Inflation moved in the wrong direction in September. Consumer prices rose 3.7% over the past year, up from 3.4% in August, while gasoline prices jumped 9.1% in just one month.

For families across South Texas, higher fuel prices mean more than paying extra at the pump. Truck drivers, farmers, ranchers, and small businesses are also dealing with higher operating costs, which can lead to higher prices for the goods and services families depend on every day.

Families are already stretching their paychecks to cover groceries, housing, utilities, and health care. Congress needs to focus on bringing these costs down and providing relief to working families and small businesses.

I will continue working with Republicans and Democrats to address rising costs, support South Texas workers and businesses, and help families keep more of their hard-earned money.
